sources.entry: InvoicePlane - Manage quotes, invoices, payments and customers for your small business. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: InvoicePlane is a self-hosted PHP web application for managing invoices, quotes, clients, and payments for small businesses.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a libre, self-hosted web app for creating, sending, and managing invoices and quotes. It keeps client records with contact details and transaction history, and maintains products and tasks/projects that can be added to invoices. Payment tracking includes monitoring payments, setting up reminders, and integrating with multiple payment gateways. It also offers template, theme, and settings customization plus financial reporting. Custom invoice and quote templates are registered through an allowlist in ipconfig.php, and the README notes that sessions can be stored at a configurable path.
use_cases: Track client payments and send reminders
Maintain a product and task catalogue for billing
Generate financial reports for a small business
Run a self-hosted billing system instead of a SaaS invoicing service
how_to_run: docker compose up -d --build (development/testing only; uses a fixed ENCRYPTION_KEY and DB password)
Production: download the latest release, upload files to the web server
Copy ipconfig.php.example to ipconfig.php and set base URL and database credentials
Navigate to the app URL in a browser to run the installer
Container deployment: configure via environment variables (see Container (Docker) Deployment Instructions)
stack: MySQL or other database (named in config, not specified in README)
notable: Custom templates are loaded from an explicit allowlist in ipconfig.php rather than scanning the filesystem
Pre-built container image configured entirely through environment variables, running migrations on startup
Optional SESS_SAVE_PATH setting to keep session files outside the web root
Removable index.php from URLs via mod_rewrite and a config flag
Formal security advisories and a CHANGELOG/UPGRADE guide for each release
caveats: Support is community-run on a best-effort basis (Discord, forums, issue tracker)
The docker compose setup is for local development only and ships a fixed encryption key and database password
Setting SESS_SAVE_PATH to an empty value breaks sessions and login; /tmp should be avoided on systemd distros
